title: sign.rs/encrypt.rs: unwrap_or_default silently drops base64 chunks
description: sign.rs wrap_base64 (line 292) and encrypt.rs build_mime (line 429) both call core::str::from_utf8(chunk).unwrap_or_default() on base64-encoded output. Base64 output is always ASCII, so the error path is unreachable. But unwrap_or_default() on the impossible error branch silently returns an empty string, which would corrupt the encoded output without any indication. The comment says 'BASE64 output is ASCII-only, so from_utf8 never fails' — which is exactly when you should use unwrap() or expect() to preserve that invariant as a panic rather than silently drop output. Suggested rewrite: replace unwrap_or_default() with .expect("base64 output is always ASCII") to make the invariant load-bearing.
